proyectos.title: Projects
proyectos.summary: FructoScan, two university projects I extended, and this village.
proyectos.intro: Four stalls, and you can check every claim in them: the live app, the tests or the measurements.

items.name: FructoScan
items.text: Scan a product's barcode at the supermarket and it tells you whether it suits you if you have fructose intolerance, and why. I built it because I have it and I was tired of shopping by reading labels one by one.
highlights: A verdict for your profile (malabsorption, hereditary intolerance or FODMAP), with fructose and sorbitol rated separately.
If the product isn't in Open Food Facts, it reads the ingredients from a photo with on-device OCR.
Looks up medicines in the official Spanish registry (AEMPS) and checks their excipients.
No accounts and no server: data stays on the phone. Works offline, has 64 tests and deploys itself to Cloudflare Pages.

items.name: University management
items.text: A Jakarta EE web app to manage degrees, courses, students and classrooms, with a REST API that does everything the website does.
highlights: Real business rules: nobody can enrol beyond the available places, and a course only goes to a classroom that fits its students.
MySQL with Flyway migrations, an audit log and the API documented in OpenAPI; a test fails if the code and the spec drift apart.
42 integration tests plus 4 against a real MySQL with Testcontainers. CI rejects anything under 75 % coverage.
The whole thing starts with Docker Compose.

items.name: Parallel gradients
items.text: Computes gradients and Jacobians in C three ways, sequentially, with OpenMP across the CPU cores and with CUDA on an RTX 5070, and checks every result against the exact derivative.
highlights: Re-running the benchmarks showed that the "173 times faster" in my original report was really about 32, so I corrected it.
Changing the algorithm beat parallelising: the per-term method is about 470 times faster than the direct one.
I tried dropping to FP32 expecting a speed-up. It gained no time and lost five orders of magnitude of precision, so it stays in FP64.
Python bindings, sanitizers, cppcheck and 93 % coverage in CI. The results can be explored on an interactive page.

items.name: The village (this portfolio)
items.text: This very portfolio: a pixel-art village with a map designed in Tiled, villagers with their own routes and animations, and content in two languages. All the text lives in JSON, so adding to it never means touching the code.
highlights: A 52 × 36 tile map with weather, animals and villagers who chat on their own.
Works on mobile, and everything can be read without playing from "Read the profile".

proyectos.note: All the code is on GitHub. I reworked both university projects after handing them in, to leave them the way I would present them at a company.
